regressions.title: Post-polish coverage check ignores placed_text, so narrative polish is rejected with a spurious report entry whenever a placed transcript is paraphrased
regressions.evidence: Generation now treats step-placed transcript text as coverage (src/pipeline/narrative.py:46 -> src/pipeline/claim_coverage.py:64), so a placed claim gets no [verify] blockquote. After polish, server.py:1381 calls validate_claim_coverage(md_narrative_text or '', claims) which has no placed_text parameter (claim_coverage.py:78-89): a placed-but-paraphrased claim is neither in the narrative nor [verify]-flagged, so with [polish].enabled every such claim lands in report['polish_rejected_claim_coverage'] and the narrative rewrite is discarded (:1382-1384). Before the diff those claims carried [verify] lines inside narrative_text, so the check passed. Static trace; no test covers paraphrasing narrative + placed transcript + polish enabled (test_successful_narrative_stage_does_not_reflag_placed_claims at tests/pipeline/test_server.py:1609 runs without polish). Polish is off by default.

regressions.title: Capture-mode narration polish can drop a claim whose only coverage was the placed narration, with no [verify] fallback
regressions.evidence: Narration is still a polish item (src/pipeline/polish.py:383-385, 474-475); the post-polish restore at server.py:1331-1332 applies only when verbatim_narration (photo mode, :1258), and the step gate at :1333-1347 inspects new['text'] only. With a placed transcript the narrative stage counts the claim as covered via placed_text and emits no [verify] line (:972-975), so if polish's _field_gate accepts a narration rewrite that drops the clause, the claim is absent from narrative, narration and the sidecar; :1381-1384 only reverts the narrative, which never contained it. Pre-diff the claim had a [verify] blockquote in narrative_text. Requires [polish].enabled (default off) and a capture transcript.

regressions.title: Held finding F-04's remedy landed under F-02 (placed_text), flipping two existing test expectations
regressions.evidence: test_real_capture_session_with_json_transcript_extracts_claims_not_raw_json now asserts md.count('[verify]') == 0 (was 3), and tests/pipeline/test_webui_pages.py:406 now expects 'Verify claims' yellow (was green). The placed_text extension is named in PLAN.json's F-02 approach text, so it is planned, but it is exactly part (3) of F-04 which .audit/fix/PLAN_UNRESOLVED.md records as held pending the user's decision. The CLAUDE.md invariant (every claim rendered or [verify]-flagged) still holds because the claim text is under its step.

regressions.title: Photo semantic rescue still runs polish_narration and may report nar-* verify claims for text that is rendered verbatim
regressions.evidence: _generate_photo calls _run_semantic_pipeline with the default polish=True (:1113-1114), so stage 2 polish_narration runs (:1678-1688) and its dropped-clause verify_claims land in placement_meta; captioned steps then render the raw pre-polish slice from `verbatim` (:1126), while :1217-1223 still merges placement_meta['verify_claims'] into the sidecar. A clause the document shows verbatim can thus be listed as needing verification, and the stage-2 LLM call is wasted for captioned steps. Uncaptioned steps still use the polished per_step as step text (:1122), so the two step kinds are inconsistent.
